public_rationale: Subsequent releases and deployments are consistent with continued existence, useful applications, and cheaper options. They do not settle an indefinite forecast about what happens 'in the end'. No decisive event meets the early-resolution rule.
limitations: The deployment and efficiency evidence is vendor-reported.
A cheaper option is not proof that every model or workload becomes cheaper.
The forecast has no completion date.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs will continue to exist, get cheaper, and have some utility.

statement.excerpt: In the end LLMs will continue to exist, no matter what; they will get cheaper. And they will find some utility (indeed they are already have).
statement.document_title: Three years on, ChatGPT still isn't what it was cracked up to be – and it probably never will be

our_interpretation: Read this as a long-term forecast of persistence, declining comparable-use prices, and at least some practical benefit.
Cheaper means a lower price for comparable capability and workload, rather than merely a smaller model or a promotional offer.
Some utility requires a useful deployment or measured benefit; it does not require usefulness on every task.
The parenthetical acknowledges existing utility but does not supply a deadline for the forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence over the intended long-term horizon establishes continuing availability, lower comparable-use prices, and practical utility. Finite observations can support these components without settling indefinite persistence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive irreversible event makes continued LLM existence impossible, or establishes that a necessary component cannot occur.

evidence.excerpt: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite outperforms 2.5 Flash in speed and quality.
evidence.explanation: The release documents continued availability and a claimed improvement in capability and efficiency. A vendor comparison at one date does not establish the full long-term forecast.

evidence.excerpt: The core of its text-channel AI agent runs on Flash-Lite.
evidence.explanation: Google describes a customer-service deployment and lower costs against comparable thinking-tier models on the same token mix. This is evidence consistent with practical utility and cheaper options, but it is vendor-reported and not a longitudinal market-wide comparison.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A stated horizon would allow a finite test using matched prices and deployment outcomes. Without one, only a decisive event meeting the early-resolution rule can close the whole forecast.
